clue.text: Black cricketer

definitions.meaning: to black something is to refuse to deal with it, as a union blacks goods
Geoffrey, the Yorkshire and England opening batsman

explanation.surface: A description of a dark-skinned cricket player.
explanation.definitionFit: To black a firm is to shun it in protest; Geoffrey of that surname opened the batting for England.

clue.text: In order to see dragonflies, a fellow hid in long grass earlier

indicators.note: the grass with the fellow inside comes before the single letter A
the fellow is concealed within the grass, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: oats are a tall cereal grass
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A man crouches in tall grass to watch dragonflies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the definition's phrasing; the definition is the zoological order itself, so 'In' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the insect order containing dragonflies and damselflies, a taxonomic rank in biology.

clue.text: See 5
Film following Jedward, say, in women's clothing

indicators.note: the film title comes after the pair, at the end

parts.note: Jedward are the Irish identical-twin pop duo John and Edward Grimes
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A movie about the pop duo Jedward dressed in women's outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching jumper and cardigan worn together, a classic item of women's knitwear.

clue.text: Manager asking for one hundred and ten percent, essentially not troubled by number being irrational

parts.note: an means one, as in 'an apple'
a ton is slang for a hundred
10 written as the letters I and O

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very centre, so take the middle letter of percent
troubled letters are disturbed and rearranged, so the word not is shuffled

parts.note: e is the irrational number, the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A demanding football manager wants maximum effort and is calm despite one player acting unreasonably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges NOT into ONT; 'essentially' takes C, the central letter of PERCENT. 'asking for' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian coach managed Chelsea Football Club when this puzzle appeared, winning the Premier League in 2017.

clue.text: Meal ordered in city (North American city, that is)

indicators.note: the rearranged meal sits inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: the letters of meal are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone orders food in a city and clarifies which one.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'city' is part of the surface; the bracketed North American city supplies NY. 'ordered' turns MEAL into AMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both introduce a clarification or a specific example, like the Latin abbreviation i.e.

clue.text: Vile smell around American seen outside Number 10, repeatedly

indicators.note: the smell and the American wrap around the number pieces, which go between them
turned around, so the two letters for body odour are read backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour
US is the United States
X is the Roman numeral for ten
ten again, this time as the digits 1 and 0 written as I and O

explanation.surface: A disgusting odour hangs around an American standing outside the Prime Minister's residence at Number 10.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses the smell; 'repeatedly' means ten is used a second time, now as digits. Number 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something offensive and highly unpleasant; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Keen to show decimal point

parts.note: decimal counting is done in tens, so 'in tens' describes it
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An eager person wants to display a decimal point.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and this word both describe feeling or showing strong, earnest enthusiasm.

clue.text: May's content as a Tory? Deny this, surprisingly

indicators.note: the words turn up in an unexpected arrangement, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is Theresa May, the Conservative Prime Minister, happy as a Tory? She would surprisingly deny it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like Theresa May; it is the month, and its content is its length. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The month of May contains that many days, so its content is a span of a month's length.

clue.text: Blue drink

definitions.meaning: to swallow a drink in one go

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling low; to sink a pint quickly is to knock it back in one.

clue.text: Lack of sense, including smell? That's being cruel

indicators.note: the senselessness holds the smell inside it

parts.note: inanity is silliness or senselessness
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Mocking someone's lack of sense, and their odour, is unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum as a stink is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cruel is the quality of lacking compassion, the noun for barbarous behaviour.

clue.text: Dog's first run out, before nap in front of number 13

indicators.note: the shortened dog word comes ahead of the nap
the nap comes ahead of the abbreviation for number
the letter is thrown out of the dog word

parts.note: a barker is a dog, so dog's gives barker's

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word run

parts.note: to doze is to nap

explanation.surface: A dog's first outing, followed by a nap before the number thirteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first run out' removes the R from BARKERS, giving BAKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional baker's count gave thirteen loaves for twelve, so this phrase names the number thirteen.

clue.text: Peaceful angler disturbed, coming across 11

indicators.note: the rearranged angler spans across the numeral, which sits inside
the angler's letters are disturbed into a new arrangement

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An angler, disturbed while fishing peacefully, sees eleven people approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' makes RELANG, which 'coming across' wraps around the Roman eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soothing and calming is peaceful; a near-synonym for tranquil.

clue.text: Chief supports old woman wearing corset

parts.note: ma is mother, informally 'old woman'
in means wearing, as in dressed in
stays are an old word for a corset

explanation.surface: The chief supports for an old woman are her corset.
explanation.definitionFit: The main ropes holding a ship's mast, hence figuratively the principal props of anything.

clue.text: Shelter from the sun, after tanning back in sun first

indicators.note: the reversed word and the sun's letter come first in the answer
the rearranged phrase follows the earlier pieces
the word in is read back to front
tanning means beating, so the letters are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sheltering from the sun after sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanning' looks like sunbathing; it means a thrashing, so THE SUN is rearranged to SENHUT. 'back' makes NI, and 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated semicircular corrugated-iron hut used as military accommodation, so a type of shelter.

clue.text: See 12
One letter Puck's forgotten is out of order

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the contracted I've is forgotten, dropped from the letter word

parts.note: a missive is a letter
the setter Puck writing of himself: Puck has, i.e. I've

explanation.surface: The setter Puck forgot a letter, which is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puck's' means 'Puck has', the setter speaking of himself: I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of order is wrong or faulty; this word means awry or inappropriate.

clue.text: Providing people to work for Chelsea now?

definitions.meaning: supplying staff or crew, as a factory is staffed
Chelsea, the US whistleblower formerly known as Bradley, now uses this surname

explanation.definitionFit: Staffing a post is to supply its crew; Chelsea, the American army whistleblower, has this surname.

clue.text: Very fine paper soon in recycling? Sort daughter binned

indicators.note: recycled material is reprocessed into new forms, so the letters are rearranged
thrown away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: kind means sort

explanation.surface: Fine paper will soon be recycled; sort it and throw a daughter's things away.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin, light, translucent writing paper named for its resemblance to the bulb's papery outer layers.

clue.text: Bad worker is laid-back and rude

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A poor employee is both lazy and impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both casual unconcern and a curt, brusque manner.

clue.text: French painter's admission

definitions.meaning: belonging to Ingres, the French neoclassical painter; his name plus possessive S spells the same letters
entry, the act of going in

explanation.surface: A French artist confesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission' looks like a confession; it means entry. The painter's name with its possessive S has exactly the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission as a means or right of entry; the word means entering a place.

clue.text: Playing duet on tablets works

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the other: the tablets come below
playing with the letters jumbles them

parts.note: E is Ecstasy, a tablet; two of them give ES

explanation.surface: Performing a duet on tablet computers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are musical studies or exercises, compositions written to practise technique.

clue.text: Designed home with escape routes?

parts.note: in means at home
having vents, outlets for air or smoke to escape

explanation.surface: A house built with escape routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devised or created originally has been designed by someone.

clue.text: Unofficial border

definitions.meaning: outside the mainstream, like the Edinburgh festival's alternative shows
an edge or decorative trim of hanging threads

explanation.definitionFit: Alternative events beside a main festival are unofficial; an edge or trim around something is its border.

clue.text: Have short article in current New Statesman

indicators.note: the shortened verb and the article go inside the current and new letters

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: cut short, missing its last letter

parts.note: to own means to have
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A reader of the New Statesman magazine takes a brief article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Statesman' looks like the magazine; 'Statesman' is read as state's man, a man from a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from a state of the American Midwest is cryptically a state's man.

clue.text: Number scored in extra time?

parts.note: a Beatles song written in music, whose title describes more time than a ... holds

explanation.surface: A football goal tally in extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a song, 'scored' means set to music, and the title describes an impossible extra-long week.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1964 Beatles hit, a musical number whose title implies more days than a week really has.

clue.text: See 26
Some things regularly interpreted as self-love

indicators.note: the letters are interpreted freely, read in a new arrangement
taking letters at regular intervals, the first, third and fifth of things

explanation.surface: Some things, regularly interpreted, reveal vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives TIG from THINGS; with SOME, these are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-regard and conceit, an obsession with oneself, amounts to self-love.

clue.text: Quality shown by 13 with Dead Head after too much drug intake

indicators.note: the dead and head pieces come after the overdose

parts.note: OD is an overdose
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A Grateful Dead fan, a Deadhead, overdoes the drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead Head' looks like a fan of the band; it is two pieces. 13 is not divisible by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is an odd number, so the property it shows is being not even.
